newsitem.title: JAPAN: Australia prime minister Howard arrives in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Australia prime minister Howard arrives in Japan.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard arrived in Japan on Wednesday for a four-day visit after winding up a three-day tour of Indonesia.
Howard will meet Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Trade Minister Shunpei Tsukahara, Emperor Akihito and business leaders while in Japan.

The visit threatens, however, to be overshadowed by a growing dispute with Beijing over Howard's planned meeting with Tibet's exiled leader, the Dalai Lama, as well as news of a ban imposed by Australia's Maritime Union on Indonesian shipping.
Howard travelled to Indonesia on Monday on his first major overseas tour to allay concerns over his conservative government's commitment to the Asian region.

The conservative Australian prime minister had planned to make his first foreign visit to Japan and Indonesia earlier in August to underscore his regional commitment, but was forced to put off the trips when his wife, Janette, needed a major operation.
Japan is Australia's largest trading partner. Bilateral trade between Australia and Japan was worth A$29.1 billion (US$23.2 billion) in 1994/95 (July-June).

Government officials in Canberra said Howard's visit was an attempt to emphasise the importance of bilateral ties between Japan and Australia, which would be underlined with meetings on Friday with Emperor Akihito and Prime Minister Hashimoto.
The two countries have a few disputes, notably access to Japanese markets for Australian agricultural products, but Howard is not expected to pursue any of them, the officials say.
Howard said this week that he would meet Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, who is on a two-week visit to Australia, after returing from his trip to Japan.
Beijing, which views the Dalai Lama as a political activist out to split China, warned on Tuesday that foreign leaders who meet the Tibetan leader would see trade and business ties with China suffer.

Howard hopes to meet the Dalai Lama in Sydney next week if their programmes allow. The Dalai Lama has been in exile since an abortive uprising against Chinese rule in Tibet in 1959. He won the 1989 Nobel Peace prize for his peaceful campaign for Tibetan autonomy.
Australia's Maritime Union on Wednesday launched rolling bans on Indonesian shipping designed to hold up ships for 24 hours.

The union said the bans were to protest against the arrest of independent labour leaders Muchtar Pakpahan and Dita Sari and were also a response to what they described as Howard's failure to press Indonesia on human rights in Jakarta this week.
"Such kind of incidents are regretted and will harm efforts to build up relations between the two countries", Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokesman Ghaffar Fadly told Reuters.
